premises.text: Expense inputs must be completable on a phone in under three seconds
premises.evidence_span: input any expense in under three seconds

premises.text: The app never asks for credit card, bank information, or even the user's name
premises.evidence_span: We'll never ask you for your credit card or bank information, not even your name

premises.text: Gamified XP, tokens, achievements, and leveling encourage tracking, and tokens unlock sponsored deals
premises.evidence_span: we're going to make it fun and rewarding

premises.text: Smart tags rise by pattern and frequency of the user's spending habits
premises.evidence_span: Spends tracks both the pattern and frequency of my top tags and intuitively responds

premises.text: Users can set subcategory budgets and see You-Versus-Them peer spending insights
premises.evidence_span: we've gone one step farther and allowed for subcategorization

premises.text: Monetization works with companies to put the right deals in front of the right audience while the app stays free for users
premises.evidence_span: working with companies to get the right deals in front of the right audience

value.text: Budget and track money in a way that is fun and fast so users know where money goes
value.evidence_span: solve the problem of budgeting and tracking your money. Not like everybody else, but fun and fast

causal_links.evidence_span: achievements are ways that we encourage our users to do some great spending habits

notes: Bootstrap/launch timing and demo XP numbers excluded as traction. Web backup treated as a feature of the same offering and folded into capture/backup UX rather than a separate premise (v1.3.2 §4.1(5)). Proactive-engagement rhetoric folded into the fast-input/anonymous product stance. Free-for-users kept inside the deals monetization premise (price+partner structure, v1.3.1 §4.1(3)).
